clauses.text:
Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF SAMUEL J. GompERS FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FOR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Samuel J. Gom-
pers, Chief Clerk, Department of Labor, who, during the month of September, 1938,
will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service,
applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of
one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by section 204 of the Act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S. C., title 5, sec.
715a), I hereby exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for
age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939.

Executive Order 7958 of August 19, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362914, Common Crawl capture 2026-01-14T04:43:33Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7958, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on September 30, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8252 (September 14, 1939) and No. 8543 (September 18, 1940); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).
